heading: EXT. ABANDONED MISSION CHURCH - COURTYARD - SUNSET

units.text: EXT. ABANDONED MISSION CHURCH - COURTYARD - SUNSET
A crumbling adobe courtyard where a dry fountain stands at the center, cracked and filled with tumbleweed.
A bell tower leans, its bell long gone.
Long violet shadows crawl across the flagstones.
Beyond the broken wall, the desert runs to a copper horizon.
CALEB MONTOYA-HART, sixties, a widowed rancher with a weathered hat and a silver mustache, sits on the rim of the fountain with a canteen across his knees.
Beside him, his granddaughter ROSALIE, ten, in a faded blue dress and a straw hat too big for her, draws in the dust with a stick.

A little way off, an old gray mule named SAINT CHRISTOPHER stands with his head low, and a stranger, a wandering priest called FATHER EMILIO DUARTE, fifties, in a patched cassock and sandals, kneels by a small fire, boiling coffee in a tin cup.
The desert is quiet.
The coffee smells of smoke.
Father, I didn't think there was anyone left out here.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: There never is. And then there is.
units.name: FATHER EMILIO

units.text: Grandpa, why is the fountain empty?
units.name: ROSALIE

units.text: Because there's no water.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: But why did they build it?
units.name: ROSALIE

units.text: Because once there was.
units.name: FATHER EMILIO

units.text: Where did it go?
units.name: ROSALIE

units.text: That is a very good question, little one. The old ones said it went underground to rest.
units.name: FATHER EMILIO

units.text: Water doesn't rest.
units.name: ROSALIE

units.text: No? Everything rests, eventually.
units.name: FATHER EMILIO

units.text: Rosalie considers this.
She draws a long wavy line in the dust, then a second beneath it.
You've been here long?
units.name: CALEB

units.text: Some years.
units.name: FATHER EMILIO

units.text: Alone?
units.name: CALEB

units.text: Never alone.
units.name: FATHER EMILIO

units.text: He lifts the cup from the fire, blows on it, and offers it to Caleb.
Caleb studies it, takes it, and drinks.
His shoulders ease.
He passes it to Rosalie, who sips, makes a face, and hands it back.
That's terrible.
units.name: ROSALIE

units.text: Rosalie.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: She is right. It is terrible coffee. But it is warm.
units.name: FATHER EMILIO

units.text: The sun touches the horizon.
The shadows of the walls stretch over the three of them.
The mule shifts its weight and sighs.
Father, I came out to scatter my wife's ashes. I thought this was the place.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: Why here?
units.name: FATHER EMILIO

units.text: She was married here. Fifty years ago in June.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: Then it is the place.
units.name: FATHER EMILIO

units.text: Caleb takes a small tin from inside his coat.
He turns it over in his hands.
Rosalie puts down her stick and takes his free hand.
The priest crosses himself and stands.
Shall I say something?
units.name: FATHER EMILIO

units.text: Please.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: Lord, here is a woman who loved this land. Let her rest in it.
units.name: FATHER EMILIO

units.text: Caleb opens the tin.
A breeze rises across the courtyard, and with it the first of the ashes lifts, a pale ribbon curling over the dry fountain, and then drifting out through the gap in the wall toward the last light.
Bye, Grandma.
units.name: ROSALIE

units.text: The wind lifts her hat.
The mule lifts his head.
The three of them watch the ribbon of dust until it is gone.
